# RFC / Playbook: "URL-to-Astro" Migration Workflow — Pre-Build Component Quarantine, Open Architecture & Zero-JS Primitives

## 1. Executive Summary & Context

This RFC documents the analysis of Timothy Ricks' follow-up video, **"Convert Any Website To Astro"**, evaluating how live websites (e.g. Stripe.com or client WordPress sites) can be cleanly converted into Astro using only their live URL and an AI coding agent:
* **Reference Video:** [Timothy Ricks: "Convert Any Website To Astro" (YouTube Wje2UgNbnTA)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wje2UgNbnTA)

### The Core Shift: Overcoming the "All-at-Once" Failure Mode
In his first video (analyzed in Issue #1), Timothy attempted to build the whole homepage from visual mockups in one shot. The AI was overwhelmed: it created messy one-off classes, hardcoded hex colors, broke light/dark modes, and produced bloated nested wrappers.

In this second video, he applied a **disciplined, phased methodology**:
1. **Pre-Build Quarantine Pass:** Rather than building pages, he forced the AI to focus **exclusively on calibrating base components on the living styleguide** (`/example-components`) to match the target site.
2. **Component Assembly Pass:** Only after all base primitives and variables were locked did he prompt the AI to build the actual homepage.

The result was a dramatic leap in code cleanliness, reusable open components, and faithful responsiveness with zero visual debt.

---

## 2. Key Technical Findings & Patterns from the Video

### A. The "Pre-Build Component Quarantine" Gate
When converting an existing site from a URL or screenshots:
* **The Antipattern:** Prompting the agent: *"Rebuild this homepage from https://stripe.com"*. The agent immediately starts writing full-page templates with ad-hoc classes and inconsistent button paddings.
* **The Quarantine Protocol:** The prompt must strictly constrain the agent:
  > *"Inspect the live site at [URL]. Rebuild/reformat ONLY the components on our living styleguide (`src/pages/_styleguide.astro`, Issue #5) to match the target site's design language and tokens. DO NOT build any new pages or custom section components yet. Map elements to existing component variants whenever possible."*
* **Why this works:** The agent refactors buttons, inputs, typography scales, tabs, badges, and card variants in isolation. When it later builds pages, it natively composes those tested primitives instead of inventing throwaway classes.

### B. Open Components vs. Closed Monoliths
* **The Problem:** Left unguided, AI agents create monolithic "closed" components (e.g. `<StripeHero />`, `<FeatureSection />`) that hardcode inner containers, custom grid rules, and local margins. This prevents reusability and breaks global token updates.
* **The Open Architecture Rule:** Sections should be **open structural wrappers** composed of standard primitives:
  ```astro
  <!-- Preferred: Open Composable Pattern -->
  <Section variant="brand">
    <Container width="narrow">
      <Heading level="h1">...</Heading>
      <Paragraph>...</Paragraph>
      <ButtonWrapper>
        <Button variant="action">...</Button>
      </ButtonWrapper>
    </Container>
  </Section>
  ```
* Layout components must expose slots, and child elements must manage their own standard vertical rhythm rather than relying on parent section custom classes.

### C. The "Three-Mode Button" Pattern
Target sites with complex dark/light surface nesting (like Stripe) frequently require **three button patterns**, not just two:
1. **Primary Action:** Solid brand color with high-contrast text.
2. **Secondary Ghost/Outline:** Faint border transitioning to solid on hover.
3. **Inverted Contrast (Surface-Aware):** A dark button on light backgrounds that flips to a light button on dark backgrounds, allowing CTAs to sit inside contrasting hero cards or banner callouts without breaking theme toggles.

### D. Zero-JS Astro SSR Marquee / Infinite Logo Ticker
Timothy highlighted an elegant native Astro pattern for infinite logo carousels (e.g. the customer logos strip on Stripe):
* In React or standard frontend frameworks, infinite marquees duplicate DOM nodes using client-side JavaScript.
* In Astro, we can create a `<LogoTicker />` primitive using **Astro `<Fragment>`**:
  * The slot content is passed once by the editor/CMS.
  * The Astro server template renders the slot twice into two adjacent flex tracks wrapped in `<Fragment>`.
  * Pure CSS `@keyframes` handles infinite scrolling.
  * **Result:** Zero client-side JavaScript, perfect SEO, and zero hydration overhead.

### E. Asset Ingestion Guardrail (`src/assets/` vs `public/`)
* In the video, the AI initially downloaded scraped site images into `public/`.
* **The Issue:** Files in `public/` completely bypass Astro's native image service (`astro:assets` / Sharp), preventing responsive WebP/AVIF generation, layout shift prevention, and intrinsic width constraints.
* **The Rule:** The agent must be explicitly guarded to place site assets in `src/assets/` (or hydrate them into EmDash Media Library via Issue #9), never dumping unoptimized assets into `public/`.

### F. Context Window Discipline ("Keep Context Low")
* Rather than keeping one long, noisy conversation that accumulates hallucinations and outdated code, the agent workflow must actively archive or fork chat sessions:
  * Chat 1: Token & Component Calibration on Styleguide.
  * Chat 2: Macro Section Layout Assembly.
  * Chat 3: Motion & Micro-Interactions (Lenis, Tab sliders).

---

## 3. Proposed Additions to the Starter

1. **Living Styleguide Quarantine Step in `new-site-workflow`:**
   Formalize the pre-build quarantine gate in `new-site-workflow`: when migrating an existing site from a URL, Stage 4 (Component Calibration on `_styleguide.astro`) must pass before Stage 5 (Page Implementation) begins.
2. **Add Native `<LogoTicker.astro>` Component:**
   Provide a zero-JS infinite scrolling ticker primitive in `src/components/` utilizing Astro SSR `<Fragment>` duplication.
3. **Asset Ingestion Rule in `.agent/rules/`:**
   Add an explicit guard in `.agent/rules/` instructing agents to route downloaded images to `src/assets/` or the EmDash Media Library, never `public/`.

---

## 4. Acceptance Criteria & Questions for Second Agent

- [ ] `new-site-workflow` documents the "URL-to-Astro" Component Quarantine protocol.
- [ ] Starter includes a native, zero-JS `<LogoTicker.astro>` component for customer logos and partner banners.
- [ ] Agent rules explicitly forbid placing site images directly into `public/`.
- [ ] Guidance on the "Three-Mode Button" pattern added to `astro-site-design`.
